NDT training in Halifax: how it works for Halifax employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET for Halifax and Nova Scotia employers, live online or onsite at your yard, shop or hangar, under ASNT Level III oversight. There is no Atlantis training centre in Halifax. The training fits employers that certify staff to an SNT-TC-1A written practice, typically for US clients or US codes. It is separate from CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certification, and Atlantis does not claim CGSB recognition.

Halifax's NDT market is built on marine, defence and aerospace work, with a smaller energy and utilities segment. Most of it is Canadian-owned and Canadian-regulated, and CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certification issued by Natural Resources Canada's National NDT Certification Body is the normal expectation for that work. That certification requires training from an NRCan Recognized Training Organization, and Atlantis does not claim that status, so we are not the right choice for a technician whose goal is a CGSB certificate.

Where Atlantis does fit in Halifax is the smaller but real part of the market with American paperwork. That covers Nova Scotia fabricators and machine shops shipping components to US customers who audit to ASNT-based procedures, and service companies supporting US-flagged or US-owned vessels and equipment. It also covers subcontractors on defence and aerospace supply chains where the US customer's specification calls for an SNT-TC-1A programme, and inspection firms that send technicians to jobs in New England. For these employers we provide SNT-TC-1A training, examination and Level III services, and help write a written practice that sits cleanly alongside any CGSB-certified staff they also employ.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Halifax

All courses follow the SNT-TC-1A recommended body of knowledge. The employer's written practice sets formal training and experience hours. See the training requirements matrix for the recommended figures method by method.

MethodLevelsWhat Halifax employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (ultrasonic testing)I, II, IIIHull and deck plate thickness surveys during ship repair, weld inspection on steel fabrication, lamination checksLevel I: employer entry rules. Level II: Level I plus logged experience
PAUT (phased array)II, IIIWeld inspection on thick structural and pressure welds, corrosion mapping on hulls, tanks and pipingUT Level II normally first
TOFDII, IIIFlaw sizing on heavy-section welds, often paired with PAUTUT Level II normally first
RT (radiographic testing)I, II, IIIRadiography of piping and pressure welds in shipbuilding and plant work, casting inspectionCNSC exposure device rules apply separately
MT (magnetic particle)I, II, IIISurface cracks on ship structure, shafting, rudder and propulsion components, lifting gear and cranesEmployer entry rules
PT (liquid penetrant)I, II, IIIAluminium and stainless structures, non-ferrous marine fittings, aircraft componentsEmployer entry rules
VT (visual testing)I, II, IIIWeld and fit-up inspection in fabrication, condition surveys of ship structure and port infrastructureEmployer entry rules
ET (eddy current)I, II, IIIAircraft structure and fastener-hole inspection, heat exchanger and condenser tubes in marine and power plantsEmployer entry rules

UT for marine work. Ship repair runs on thickness gauging. Hull plating, decks, tanks and bulkheads are surveyed on a grid, and each reading is compared with the original scantlings. Our UT Level I and II training for Halifax candidates emphasises coated-surface technique, echo-to-echo measurement through paint, gauging from one side, and recording that fits a thickness survey report. Level II also covers angle-beam weld inspection on the thick structural steel common in naval and commercial construction.

PAUT and TOFD. Taught at Level II and III on a UT Level II foundation. Encoded scans, focal law setup and C-scan corrosion mapping work well on large hull and tank areas, and PAUT is increasingly used in place of RT for weld inspection because it avoids radiation exclusion zones in busy yards.

RT. Exposure principles, image quality, film and digital interpretation, and weld and casting discontinuities. In a shipyard or dry dock, radiography scheduling and exclusion zones are a real planning constraint, and the course covers how RT fits into a production schedule. Radiation certification in Canada is separate (see FAQ).

MT, PT and VT. In marine and defence work these methods are used every day. MT finds cracks in welded steel structure and propulsion components. PT is the go-to for aluminium superstructures and non-ferrous fittings. VT underpins everything, from weld profile to the condition of structure opened up during refit.

ET for aerospace and heat exchangers. Halifax has military and civil aircraft maintenance, and ET is the core aerospace NDT method: surface and near-surface cracks around fastener holes and in aluminium structure. The ET course covers impedance-plane analysis, probe choice and reference standards. Tube inspection techniques cover the marine and power-plant heat exchanger side. Note that aerospace NDT under a prime contractor's specification often calls for NAS 410 or EN 4179. Atlantis does not provide training under those standards. Our ET course is SNT-TC-1A-based.

Level III. Live online ASNT Level III exam preparation for candidates in Atlantic Canada.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Halifax, step by step

Under SNT-TC-1A there is no national examining body. The employer certifies, based on its own written practice. The path looks like this:

  1. Employer written practice. The foundation document: levels, training, experience, examinations, vision, certifying authority and records. See written practice development.
  2. Formal training. Classroom hours for the method and level, delivered live online, onsite or blended. Recommended hours are in the requirements matrix.
  3. Documented experience. Supervised work in the method, in the hours set by the written practice, signed off and traceable. In Halifax that often means ship-repair periods and fabrication contracts.
  4. General examination. Written, on method theory.
  5. Specific examination. Written, on the employer's procedures, equipment and applicable codes. A fabricator shipping to a US customer might be examined on AWS D1.1 or the customer's specification.
  6. Practical examination. Hands-on, on specimens with known flaws, graded by the Level III or a designee under the written practice.
  7. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, with near vision checked annually.
  8. Certification. The employer's certifying authority signs and files it.
  9. Recertification. At the interval set in the written practice. Changing employer means certifying again under the new written practice.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Halifax crews

Halifax programmes use three delivery options, none of which involves an Atlantis campus.

  • Live online. Theory and mock examinations run in instructor-led virtual sessions. Halifax is on Atlantic Time, which puts it ahead of most North American trainers, so we schedule sessions to suit Atlantic Canada working hours. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility. An instructor runs practicals and examinations at your shop, yard, dock or hangar with your equipment and specimens. Shipyard and defence sites have access and security procedures, which the employer sponsors in advance. See corporate NDT training.
  • Blended. Online theory followed by a short onsite practical and examination block.

Halifax scheduling follows the ship-repair and refit calendar, fabrication contract milestones and plant outages. Training ahead of a big refit or construction phase gives technicians time to build logged experience during the work. Tell us your project timeline and we will quote cohort or onsite delivery within one business day. Request a Halifax training quote.

Where NDT technicians work in Halifax

  • Shipbuilding and ship repair. Halifax Harbour has a major naval shipbuilding yard, plus dry-dock and repair capacity for commercial and government vessels. NDT runs at production volume here: UT, PAUT, RT, MT, PT and VT across hull, structure and systems.
  • Royal Canadian Navy. Halifax is home port of the Atlantic fleet, and naval fleet maintenance brings a steady flow of inspection on ship structure, machinery and systems. Military helicopter operations at 12 Wing Shearwater add aviation maintenance.
  • Aerospace MRO. Aircraft maintenance and aerospace defence contractors around Halifax Stanfield International Airport do heavy maintenance on military and civil aircraft, where ET, PT and UT are central.
  • Port and marine infrastructure. Container terminals, cranes, wharves and bridges across the harbour need MT, UT and VT on structures and lifting equipment.
  • Energy and utilities. Thermal generating stations in the region need boiler, piping and heat exchanger inspection during outages. Fuel storage terminals need tank and piping inspection. Nova Scotia's offshore and emerging renewable energy sectors, including offshore wind planning and tidal energy testing in the Bay of Fundy, add structural and weld inspection work.
  • Fabrication and manufacturing. Steel fabricators, machine shops and component manufacturers across Halifax Regional Municipality and the Burnside industrial park area, some shipping to US customers.

Codes and regulators. Pressure equipment in Nova Scotia is regulated provincially under the province's technical safety legislation, which uses CSA B51, and ASME Section VIII and B31.3 cover vessel and piping construction. Shipbuilding follows class-society rules and the customer's specifications, and structural welding follows CSA W59 or AWS D1.1. Aerospace follows Transport Canada or military airworthiness rules plus the prime contractor's NDT specification. Industrial radiography is regulated federally by the CNSC.

What Halifax employers typically ask for. CGSB certification is the norm for Canadian marine, defence and pressure-equipment work. Aerospace employers may add NAS 410 or EN 4179 qualification, and RT crews need CNSC exposure device certification. Security clearance matters for defence sites. SNT-TC-1A certification comes up mainly when the customer is American. For pay context, see the NDT salary guide.

Level III services and written practices for Halifax NDT companies

For a Halifax fabricator or inspection firm that has just won a US customer, the first request is often, send us your SNT-TC-1A written practice and your Level III's credentials. Atlantis helps companies answer that quickly and properly.

  • Written practice development. We write an SNT-TC-1A written practice covering the methods and levels you actually use, written to hold up in a customer audit. See written practice development.
  • Outsourced Level III. Procedure and technique sheet writing, examination preparation and grading, and audit support.
  • Specification review. We map a US customer's NDT specification to your procedures and flag where acceptance criteria, calibration or reporting need to change.
  • Two schemes, one workforce. Many Halifax firms employ CGSB-certified technicians. The written practice can define how SNT-TC-1A certification is used alongside CGSB for specific customers, so neither scheme is compromised.

Framework: SNT-TC-1A training and certification. Book a Level III consultation for your Halifax company.

Practise before the practical exam

Practical NDT is a 3D simulator where Atlantis trainees can practise 12 NDT methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. The aircraft hangar and welding workshop scenes match Halifax's aerospace and fabrication work most closely. Use it to rehearse technique and interpretation between sessions. It is not a substitute for hands-on training or the practical examination on real specimens. For written exams, see UT Level 2 practice questions.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees course content, examinations and written-practice work for Halifax programmes.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Halifax

How do I get NDT certified in Halifax?

For most Canadian marine, defence and pressure-equipment work, get CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certification through the NRCan NDT Certification Body, training with an NRCan Recognized Training Organization. If your employer uses an SNT-TC-1A written practice, it certifies you after training, logged experience, examinations and a vision test. Atlantis delivers training and Level III examinations for that route.

Can I take NDT training online in Nova Scotia?

Theory, yes. Atlantis runs live online theory at times that suit Atlantic Canada. Practical training and examination have to be hands-on and are delivered onsite at the employer's facility. See online NDT training.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Halifax employers?

Within limits. SNT-TC-1A certification is valid within the employer programme that issues it, and Halifax firms serving US customers use it. Canadian marine, defence and pressure-equipment work usually expects CGSB. Check the contract and the customer's specification.

Does Atlantis training count toward CGSB?

No. NRCan requires CGSB training from its Recognized Training Organizations, and Atlantis does not claim that status. Our training supports SNT-TC-1A programmes.

Can I get aerospace NDT training for NAS 410 in Halifax through Atlantis?

No. Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A only. Aerospace employers may require NAS 410 or EN 4179, and those need their own qualification route.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

The employer's written practice sets the formal training and experience hours. The SNT-TC-1A recommendations are in the requirements matrix. Experience usually takes longer than classroom time.

Do I need a licence for radiography in Nova Scotia?

Gamma radiography is regulated by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission. The employer holds a CNSC licence, and operators must be CNSC Certified Exposure Device Operators or trainees under the direct supervision and continuous observation of one. X-ray equipment is also subject to provincial radiation rules. Our RT course does not grant any radiation certification.

What does NDT training cost in Halifax?

Quote on request. It depends on method, level, group size, delivery model, site access requirements, and whether Level III and written-practice services are included. We respond within one business day. Ask about onsite training for your Halifax crew.

Can you run practicals at a shipyard or defence site?

Yes, where the employer sponsors access and meets the site's security and safety requirements. Practicals then run on your equipment and representative specimens.

What methods are most useful for marine work?

UT thickness gauging, MT and VT dominate ship repair. PAUT, RT and PT cover welds and non-ferrous structure. The exact mix comes from the yard's procedures and class requirements.

Can I prepare for the ASNT Level III exam from Halifax?

Yes. Level III preparation runs live online.

Our US customer asked for our written practice. Where do we start?

Start with a gap review of what you have now, then write or revise the written practice and procedures. See written practice development.
